To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a patient with acromegia and a large pituitary gland was found to have an ectopic source of growth hormone-releasing activity in a pancreatic islet cell tumor.
a patient with acromegalic signs and symptoms had a pituitary adenoma that was actually somatotroph cell hyperplasia.

a pancreatic islet GRF-secreting tumor was responsible for the acromegaly of a woman with Turner's Syndrome and that removal of this tumor resulted in a complete clinical and endocrinological remission of her condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the control of the secretion of growth hormone (GH).

the development and application of a method for the determination of GH-releasing hormone in human plasma by means of a radioimmunoassay using a specific antibody raised in rabbits against synthetic GH-releasing hormone.
the identification of the GRF from the pancreatic tumor, and the characterization of the tumor cells that synthesize and secrete this GRF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first reported case of somatotroph adenoma with acromegalic features in Turner's syndrome.
the patient presented here had acromegaly with somatotrophic hyperplasia, which was cured by removal of a GRF-secreting tumor of the pancreas.
acromegaly can occur with somatostroph hyperplasia, and the hyperplasia can be reversed to normal by removal of an ectopic GRF-producing pancreatic islet tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ectopic production of GRF can cause somatotroph cell hyperplasia and acromegalic symptoms, but that removal of the GRP source results in normalization of the pituitary gland.

acromegaly can be caused by a GRF-producing tumor, not only in the pituitary, but also in ectopic locations, and that the presence of a discrete pituitary tumor is not always required to explain the biochemical and clinical findings of acromegalic patients.
the ectopic production of GRF by a pancreatic islet cell tumor can cause GH hypersecretion, which is clinically indistinguishable from that caused by pituitary GH-secreting adenomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acromegaly may be caused by ectopic secretion of GRF, and the pituitary may be hyperplastic rather than neoplastic.
ectopic GRF is a rare cause of acromegalic symptoms, and that the diagnosis can be confirmed by demonstrating the presence of a GRF-like peptide in the ectopic tissue and in the patient's plasma.
the pituitary gland can be stimulated to release excessive amounts of GH by ectopic sources of GRF.
